ai_root_cause: VLAN 30 is missing from SW1's VLAN database, causing access port Gi0/2 to show as inactive, while interface Vlan30 is also configured with shutdown. Consequently, SW1 cannot bring up the Layer 3 interface for 192.168.30.0/24, leaving SW1 without a connected route to VLAN 30 and PC-HR unable to reach SRV-FILES.

SW1 is missing the Switched Virtual Interface (SVI) for VLAN 30 (interface Vlan30). Consequently, 192.168.30.1 does not exist on SW1, preventing SRV-ERP from reaching its default gateway and preventing SW1 from routing traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 30.

SW1 interface GigabitEthernet0/2 is incorrectly assigned to VLAN 10 (SALES) instead of VLAN 20 (HR). Because PC-HR is configured with IP address 192.168.20.30, its ARP requests for the default gateway 192.168.20.1 are broadcast onto VLAN 10, where no Layer 3 interface responds.

SW2 interface GigabitEthernet0/24 allowed VLAN list is configured to allow only VLAN 10, pruning VLAN 20 traffic across the uplink. As a result, hosts in VLAN 20 attached to SW2 cannot reach their gateway on SW1.

There is a native VLAN mismatch on the Gi0/24 trunk link between SW1 and SW2. SW1 is configured with native VLAN 1 while SW2 is configured with native VLAN 99, causing CDP mismatch warnings and untagged traffic leakage.

PC-ACC is configured with an incorrect default gateway IP address (192.168.50.254). The actual Layer 3 interface on R1 for the 192.168.50.0/24 subnet is GigabitEthernet0/0 with IP address 192.168.50.1. Because no device responds to ARP for 192.168.50.254, PC-ACC cannot forward off-subnet traffic to the server LAN (192.168.60.0/24).

PC-BRANCH is configured with an invalid default gateway IP address (192.168.7.1) due to a typographical error. Because 192.168.7.1 is outside PC-BRANCH's local subnet (192.168.70.0/24), the host operating system cannot determine a local route or ARP for the gateway, resulting in immediate local reachability failure.

PC-LAB is missing a valid default gateway setting (currently configured as 0.0.0.0), so its operating system cannot install a default route to forward off-subnet traffic destined for 192.168.40.10 to SW-CORE (192.168.41.1).

PC-FIN has its default gateway set to 192.168.80.50 (the print server SRV-PRINT) instead of the actual router gateway address 192.168.80.1 on R3. Because SRV-PRINT is an end host that does not perform Layer 3 routing, any off-subnet packets destined for 192.168.81.0/24 are sent to SRV-PRINT and dropped.

PC-SUP is configured with a /25 subnet mask (255.255.255.128) instead of the correct /24 subnet mask (255.255.255.0). As a result, PC-SUP treats any host in VLAN 90 with an IP address above 192.168.90.127 (such as 192.168.90.200) as off-subnet and routes traffic for them through its default gateway rather than resolving them via ARP locally.

The DHCP pool STAFF-POOL on SW-DHCP is misconfigured with network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 instead of 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0. Because SW-DHCP's Vlan100 interface is in 192.168.100.0/24, SW-DHCP cannot find a matching DHCP pool for incoming DHCP requests from VLAN 100 clients, causing PC-NEW's request to time out.

DHCP pool LAB-POOL on R-CAMPUS is configured with default-router 192.168.111.1, which is outside the local 192.168.110.0/24 subnet. As a result, PC-LEASED receives an unreachable default gateway address, preventing it from sending traffic off-subnet.

The DHCP configuration on SW-BR has a typographical error in the excluded-address setting ('192.168.12.1' instead of excluding 192.168.120.50). Because 192.168.120.50 was not excluded from pool BRANCH-POOL, SW-BR assigned it to PC-TEMP via DHCP, causing an IP address conflict with statically configured server SRV-APP.

SW-CAMP interface Vlan130 is missing an 'ip helper-address 192.168.131.10' configuration after being reloaded from an older configuration file. Because the DHCP server resides on a different subnet (VLAN 131), DHCP broadcast requests from clients in VLAN 130 are not forwarded across the Layer 3 boundary.

The DHCP pool TILL-POOL on SW-RETAIL is configured with an incorrect DNS server IP address (192.168.140.253), which does not exist in the topology. PC-TILL receives this invalid DNS server setting via DHCP, causing all domain name resolution attempts to time out despite having full Layer 3 connectivity to the actual DNS server (SRV-DNS at 192.168.141.53).

PC-USER is configured to use 192.168.150.1 (the default gateway SVI on SW-OFFICE) as its primary DNS server rather than the actual DNS server SRV-DNS at 192.168.150.50. Because SW-OFFICE does not host a DNS service, name queries sent to 192.168.150.1 time out despite full Layer 3 reachability to SRV-DNS.

PC-USER is configured with an invalid DNS server address of 10.10.10.53, which is unreachable and does not exist in the network. The actual DNS resolver is SRV-DNS at 192.168.160.50, which is active and reachable via ICMP from PC-USER.
PC-USER lacks a DNS server configuration, preventing it from resolving domain names to IP addresses. Network connectivity at Layer 3 to the DNS server at 192.168.170.50 is fully operational.

GigabitEthernet0/2 on SW-DEPOT, which connects to DNS server SRV-DNS (192.168.180.50), is administratively down. This breaks physical connectivity to the DNS server, causing all name resolution requests from clients in VLAN 180 to fail.

IP routing is disabled globally on multilayer switch SW-L3. Because IP routing is not enabled, SW-L3 acts purely as a Layer 2 switch and will not forward packets between Vlan210 (192.168.210.0/24) and Vlan211 (192.168.211.0/24), despite both SVIs being configured and operationally up.

R-EDGE is missing a default route or static route pointing to ISP router R-ISP (203.0.113.1). Because R-EDGE lacks a route for destination network 198.51.100.0/24, it drops outgoing traffic from PC-OFFICE destined for SRV-PORTAL (198.51.100.10).
